unsupported_claims: LINE(1st+2nd) is applied to the language network as a fully unsupervised method
When the two embeddings are combined, the dimension weights can be tuned from unlabeled data, e.g. via held-out edge reconstruction or link prediction
The method is fully unsupervised so LINE(1st+2nd) handles unsupervised tasks, which contradicts the paper's statement that it is only applied to supervised tasks
rationale: The answer accepts the false premise and claims that weights for LINE(1st+2nd) can be tuned from unlabeled data. The paper says weighting is hard in unsupervised tasks, so LINE(1st+2nd) is applied only to supervised ones. The generic description of first- and second-order proximity is correct, but it does not rescue the core claim.
